card.title: Exam bank — every board question on lenses

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Two questions: lens-maker derivation for convex lens (2022, 5 marks: two-surface refraction chain) and the f = 15 cm real double-size image numerical (2023: object 22.5 cm, image 45 cm out). Power adds in contact (dioptre = 1/m).

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: maker: 1/f = (mu - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2) · lens: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u · m = v/u · P = 1/f(m), contact P = P1 + P2

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Thin-lens paraxial approximations (meaning thick lenses shift principal planes). Cartesian signs fixed once (light left to right). Maker formula assumes air surroundings (immersion rescales to relative index).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Real 2x image: m = -2, so v = -2u; with f = 15: 1/15 = -3/2u gives u = -22.5 cm, v = -45 cm. Equiconvex glass mu = 1.5: f = R. Plano-convex halves the power.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2023 (4): m = v/u = -2 (real, inverted). 1/f = 1/v - 1/u becomes 1/15 = -1/2u - 1/u = -3/2u, so u = -22.5 cm, v = -45 cm. NEB 2022 (5): refract at surface one, feed image to surface two, thin limit cancels thickness, maker formula appears.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: sign chaos (fix Cartesian first); real-image m sign (negative); maker formula applied to immersed lenses without relative index. Real lenses add chromatic/spherical aberration beyond the formula.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: The asked derivation: n2/v - n1/u = (n2-n1)/R at surface one, chain into surface two, thin-lens limit kills thickness. Power combination follows from stacked deviations (contact only).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Power in dioptre = 100/f(cm). Converging positive f, diverging negative. Real images: m negative. 'Derive maker' means the two-surface chain, never the memorised end.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2022 (5): maker formula derivation (convex). NEB 2023 (4): f = 15 cm real 2x image positions. That is the complete bank.
